records.issue_text: Salesforce uses response.statusText !== "OK" check which is unreliable for HTTP/2 (empty statusText); should use response.ok
records.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts` the new refresh flow does `if (response.statusText !== "OK") throw new HttpError(...)`. This is a brittle correctness check: `statusText` can be empty or differ across fetch implementations/protocols (including HTTP/2), which could cause throwing on a successful 2xx response. Using `response.ok` (or `response.status`) would be the reliable success predicate.

records.issue_text: Zoho Bigin passes credentialId as the userId to refreshOAuthTokens instead of credential.userId
records.rationale: In `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the new `refreshOAuthTokens` helper is called with `credentialId` as the third argument: `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)`. However, `refreshOAuthTokens` is defined to take `userId: number | null` as its third parameter, and other integrations consistently pass `credential.userId`. Passing a credential id instead of the user id will cause the sync-path request payload (`calcomUserId`) to be wrong when credential sharing is enabled.

records.issue_text: Webhook handler uses .parse instead of safeParse so malformed input causes unhandled 500 errors
records.rationale: In the newly added webhook route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the request body is validated with `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body);` without any surrounding try/catch. `zod.parse()` throws on malformed input, which would result in an unhandled exception and a 500 response instead of a controlled 4xx (e.g., 400).

records.issue_text: Webhook handler lacks req.method restriction, so GET with garbage body hits the same parse path
records.rationale: New API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` has no `req.method` guard (e.g., `if (req.method !== 'POST') ...`). The handler always runs header secret check and then unconditionally does `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)`, so a `GET` (or other non-POST) request with missing/garbage body will still hit the same parse path and can throw, resulting in an unintended error path (likely 500) instead of a proper 405/validation response.

records.issue_text: Webhook secret compared with plain !== string comparison instead of crypto.timingSafeEqual, vulnerable to timing attacks
records.rationale: In the newly added webhook handler `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the secret check is implemented with a direct inequality comparison: `req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` and returns 403 on mismatch. This is a plain string comparison (not constant-time) and matches the finding that it should use something like `crypto.timingSafeEqual` to avoid timing side-channel leakage when comparing shared secrets.
records.stripped_text: Webhook secret compared with plain !== string comparison instead of crypto.timingSafeEqual, vulnerable to timing attacks

records.issue_text: APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is typed string | undefined instead of boolean, risking misbehavior in boolean-typed consumers and accidental truthiness edge cases
records.rationale: In `packages/lib/constants.ts`, `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is defined as `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY;`, which in TS has the inferred type `string | undefined` (because `&&` returns one of the operands). The new consumers in this diff use it in truthiness checks (e.g., `if (!APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED)`), so it works at runtime, but the finding is correct that it is not a boolean and can create type/truthiness edge cases for any boolean-typed consumers of this exported constant.
